import numpy as np

def dynamics(t, x, u):
    i_L = x[0]  # inductor current (A)
    v_out = x[1]  # output voltage (V)
    D = u[0]  # duty cycle (0 to 1)
    V_in = 12.0  # input voltage (V)
    V_out_target = 48.0  # target output voltage (V)
    R_L = 0.1  # inductor ESR (ohm)
    R_C = 0.05  # capacitor ESR (ohm)

    # Inductor dynamics
    di_L_dt = (V_in - v_out) / R_L  # change in inductor current (A/s)

    # Output voltage dynamics
    dv_out_dt = (D * V_in - v_out) / (R_C + R_L)  # change in output voltage (V/s)

    dx = np.array([di_L_dt, dv_out_dt])
    return dx
